added: New servers take the next free port (25566, 25567…) when 25565 is already used by another server or program.
The agent's conversation list can be folded away.
changed: The port setting is now called Connection port, and the query and RCON ports say they are not for joining. A port clash on start says where to change it.
The 'applies on the next start' note in server settings is a small line next to the search box.

added: Agent chats: keep several conversations per server in a list on the left, start a new one, rename or delete them; chats keep working in the background while you look at another.
The agent shows its todo list above the message box, and its questions take your own answer with Other.
Switching between server tabs returns each server to where you left it, down to the plugin settings or the add-content page.
changed: Back and forward also remember tabs inside a page: log views, settings categories, plugin settings, the map, player lists and an open backup.
Page titles are gone and their buttons moved into the rows below, so content starts higher. The player name box both adds and finds players.
When a long agent chat is summarized, the summary shows as a folded card, and the agent keeps answering in Korean.

added: Git tab: for servers kept in git, see changed files line by line, commit the ones you pick, browse history, restore a file and pull or push. Start git sets up a repository with a .gitignore that leaves out worlds, logs and jar files.
Edit text files right in the SFTP window, on either side, and save them back.
The Claude agent can use git too: see changes, read diffs and history, commit and restore files, on local and SSH servers.
The agent offers server setup and a security check, with different starter buttons for Minecraft and other game servers.
changed: Backups leave out the .git folder unless you turn it on in Settings.
Number settings show their unit inside the same box.
Clearer Korean error messages.
fixed: Server downloads that stall (new Purpur builds can be slow at first) continue from where they stopped instead of starting over.

added: Plugin and mod settings: config files are found on their own and shown as a form with switches and fields, or opened right there in the code editor.
Integrations tab for EssentialsX, LuckPerms and plugins that describe themselves with monolab.json or the Monolab add-on API.
Open more kinds of files: decompiled .class files, what's inside .jar and .zip files, NBT data, images, and a 3D view for .bbmodel models.
Browse the files inside a backup, compare them with the server, and restore only the ones you pick.
Back up worlds only.
Server groups on the home screen, with start all and stop all.
Change a server's core between Paper, Purpur, Leaf and Folia, or from Vanilla to one of them.
A Velocity proxy can connect servers on this PC, on the same SSH host, or SSH servers from a local proxy. Forwarding is set up for you.
Advanced mode in the Resources tab: tick times, memory areas, garbage collection, threads and CPU per core (add-on 34 or later).
Install another app version from Settings.
Add-on settings: turn the live map, web map, inventories and other add-on features on or off from the app.
Save the visible map as a PNG, send a player to a spot on the map, and share a map link that opens at the same place and height.
The player window shows the ender chest beside the inventory, with durability bars under damaged items.
Back and forward buttons in the Files tab.
The home screen shows total CPU use for each session.
Choose which folders and files go into a backup.
changed: Page titles and tabs stay in place while only the content scrolls.
Chunk filters on the map no longer lag and move together with the map; the map uses less CPU.
The console side panel can be folded, and its numbers open the matching tab.
"Later" on the update notice hides it until the app restarts.
Adding a player to the whitelist no longer asks for confirmation.
Korean text is clearer, and error messages say what happened and what to do.
Plugin pages and the Integrations tab use the space better.
The home screen shows summary tiles on top, uptime on running servers, and when stopped servers last ran.
Plugin lists, logs, the disk dialog and server settings scroll inside their own box.
Starter prompts in the Claude agent are sent in English, which uses fewer tokens.
fixed: Saplings, beds, shields and shelf mushrooms show proper icons in inventories.
Paper servers no longer warn about legacy material support (add-on 35).
The size column in the Files tab lines up with its header.
The chunk pre-generation install button showed a wrong word in Korean.

added: The web map can pick a map height too, like the app (add-on 32).
Pumpkin servers show how far a map height layer has been drawn.
changed: The world map uses much less memory, especially when zoomed far out, and map tiles reach the screen faster.
The Claude agent can change part of a file instead of rewriting it, and reads big files in parts, using less of your plan.
The Claude chat stays smooth while answers stream in, and long conversations open faster.
One Manage sessions button on the home screen; adding a panel looks like adding an SSH server.
The installer is about 2.6 MB smaller.
fixed: The console no longer jumps while you read older lines as new ones arrive.
Escape closes open popups.

added: Pumpkin servers get a world map: with add-on 31, the places players walk through are drawn and colored from the game's textures.

Choose the map height: point at the layers button on the map and slide to a Y level to see caves and floors below it. The far right end is the normal surface map. This replaces the cave toggle and needs add-on 31.
Pumpkin servers show entity counts by type in the Monitor tab.
changed: Inside a server, the server tabs move up into the top bar and the server buttons sit at the top right, leaving more room for the page.
The server tool list is a wider list grouped into Server, Manage and Status, with clearer icons. Point at the app icon at the top left to fold it down to icons.
The Quick run button is gone from the top bar. Ctrl+K still opens it.
fixed: After stopping a server, add-on install and update still asked to stop the server until the tab was reopened.
Dragging a server card also selected text.
Layout fixes: console status cards on narrow windows, Monitor cards and numbers, file table headers, the server creation summary and wider console margins.

added: The world map updates live: with add-on 30, blocks players change show up in the app and web map within a few seconds, without waiting for the server to save.
Saved player items can be changed or deleted while the server is stopped: click a slot in the player details. The old file is kept as a backup.
fixed: The Save and Roll back buttons in the file editor looked like plain text and a square box.
Files with Windows line breaks showed as modified as soon as they were opened, and saving changed their line breaks.
Binary files such as .class opened in the editor as garbled text. They are now refused.
The memory shown in the console status panel differed from the Monitor tab. Both now show Java heap memory.

added: Leaf server core: pick it when creating a server, with plugins, the Monolab add-on and spark like Paper.
fixed: SSH servers in the same parent folder shared one backup list, so restoring or cleaning old backups could touch another server. Each server now keeps its own backups.

changed: The Trash is in the top menu, next to Settings.
fixed: Text fields showed two outlines when focused. Now the field border lights up once.
Creating a server from a modpack ignored the SSH server chosen under Create on and made it on this PC.

added: A new look: a menu across the top, tabs for the servers you have open, an icon rail inside each server and a status panel on the right of the console.
Right-click menus with the actions for the place you clicked: servers, text fields, links and the page itself.
Snapshot versions can be shown when creating a server or changing its version.
Player details show the ender chest and, on hover, each item's name, enchantments and durability.
With add-on 29, a running server shows what online players are carrying right now, refreshed every 5 seconds.
Importing a folder with a Terraria, Valheim or other game server recognises the game and sets it up.
changed: Every tab has been redesigned, and creating a server goes step by step: game, core, version, then a summary.
After three failed tries in a row the app stops reconnecting to an SSH host until you press Reconnect.
The Pumpkin add-on supports Pumpkin 0.2.1.
fixed: The server list and settings could be lost if the app closed while saving. Data files are now written safely and restored from a backup copy if damaged.
A server whose folder was deleted showed a confusing Windows error and could not be removed from the list. It now shows "Folder missing" and can be removed.

Tunnel helpers (Cloudflare, playit) kept running after the app closed by an update or a crash, so addresses stayed open and duplicate tunnels piled up. They are stopped before an update and cleaned up on the next start.
changed: The Network tab shows each address as its own card, with the server's protocol and port.
playit is turned on and off from the Network tab; the button above the console is gone.

added: A Network tab for each server: every address friends can use (this PC, same Wi-Fi, playit), the playit card, and router port forwarding steps for the server's protocol.
playit works for UDP: custom program servers choose TCP, UDP or both, and game servers (Terraria, Valheim, Palworld and more) open the right ports.
changed: The agent spends less of your plan each turn without changing what it can do.
The app starts faster: the code editor, agent, panel admin and SFTP load only when opened.
Resources for game and custom program servers show only CPU and memory.
fixed: Custom program servers started from a .bat or Ruby/Python script showed an empty console.
Stopping a .bat server no longer stops at "Terminate batch job (Y/N)?".
Terraria stops cleanly instead of being killed.
The playit button in the console header was cut off.

added: Servers for other games: Terraria, Valheim, Palworld, Project Zomboid, Rust, Satisfactory, 7 Days to Die, ARK and FiveM, with install size and free space shown before creating.
Custom program servers: run any server program from a folder you choose.
The world map web page now runs inside the Monolab add-on on its own port, like BlueMap, with player faces and a button that copies a link to the spot you're looking at.
Datapacks: browse and install from Modrinth, add a zip, and remove what a world has.
Server numbers next to the console: CPU, memory, TPS, players, disk use and the players online.
Pterodactyl and Pelican panels work next to Hydrodactyl. The panel type is detected when you test or save.
A compact list option in Settings.
changed: A more readable look: higher contrast, larger text and a calmer monochrome theme.
Creating a server goes step by step: game, core, then version.
The web map loads much faster: tiles are drawn ahead in the background, connections are reused and unchanged tiles aren't sent again. Zooming glides smoothly.
The agent uses less of your plan and follows the system language.
Bigger sidebar icons.
fixed: Status dots on collapsed sidebar tiles are no longer cut off.
Requests to Pterodactyl and Pelican panels used Hydrodactyl-only paths, so starting servers, the console and files failed.
removed: Sharing the map through the web panel's Cloudflare address. The add-on serves the map itself now.

added: Serves the world map web page on its own port, draws zoomed-out views ahead of time and shows the faces of players online.
The Worlds tab opens straight to a full-size map, with dimensions, players and bookmarks, and tools in small menus on the map.
Right-drag on the map to select an area: generate its chunks, see how long players stayed there, copy its corners, save it as a PNG or delete its chunks.
Share the world map with friends as a web page through the web panel's Cloudflare address.
Chunksmith can be installed and used for chunk generation, next to Chunky.
Chunk borders on the map, with chunk and region file under the cursor.
Offline players' last positions on SSH and panel servers too.
Pumpkin servers can be created on SSH servers.
Chunk cleanup takes any number of minutes.
A warning before closing the app while the web panel is on.
changed: The map loads much faster: drawn tiles are kept on disk, blurry tiles fill gaps while loading, and the map zooms out two more steps.
Map views read small stats files from addon 27 instead of whole region files, and remember what they read.
The agent uses much less of your plan when restarting servers and reading the console.
Monitor is now Resources, and disk usage moved there.
Picking your own server jar is now a card in the core list.
fixed: The console no longer stops a little above the newest line when opened.
Checking the addon on SSH servers no longer hashes every mod file.
Map tiles drawn without colors were sometimes saved and showed as black squares.
Loaded chunks are visible when the map is zoomed far out.

added: Writes small per-region stats files (time players stayed, entities, generation status and more) next to the map tiles, so map views load quickly.
Pre-generate chunks with Chunky from the Worlds tab — install, start, pause and follow progress in the app.
Disk usage for a server: what takes up space, plus one-click cleanup of old logs, crash reports and memory dumps.
World map views: time players stayed, last saved, entities, block entities, size, generation status and data version per chunk.
Scheduled restarts can warn players in game: choose when, how (chat, tellraw or title) and what to say.
The agent screen shows which Claude and Codex account is signed in (name, email and plan).
changed: The Worlds tab lists every world and dimension in one flat list.
The agent uses much less of your plan: start and restart wait for the server and return a short summary, and console reads only return new lines.
Bookmarks made by clicking the map use the real ground height.
The chunk cleanup notice for SSH servers says the whole server folder is backed up first.
fixed: SSH servers with crash restart no longer hide why a server stopped right after starting.
Stopping an SSH or panel server from its console or in game was recorded as a crash in Run history.
Chunk cleanup could leave old mobs and item frames behind if a side file couldn't be read.
Chunk cleanup couldn't be applied to a server that had crashed.
Mod update warnings said a needed mod was missing when it was installed by hand.
Dragging the world map, or right-clicking it, could open the bookmark window.
The loaded chunk list no longer gets in the way on servers that can't provide it, such as Folia.

added: Loaded chunks on the world map — blue for loaded, orange for force-loaded (needs addon 25).
Chunk cleanup in the Worlds tab: removes chunks players barely stayed in to make worlds smaller, with a backup first.
Run history in the Logs tab: starts, stops and crashes with exit code and uptime.
SSH servers can restart themselves after a crash, even while the app is closed.
Save the world map as a PNG, and click the map to add a bookmark.
Compare a server's start settings, server.properties and mods with another server.
Update warnings when a new mod version needs a mod you don't have or clashes with one you have.
Keep only the newest scheduled backups (Settings).
Quick-start cards in the agent chat, and the agent can install or update the Monolab addon.
changed: The agent signs in inside the app only and no longer borrows the Claude or Codex sign-in on this computer. Sign in once in the Agent tab.
Panel servers show Disconnected instead of Stopped when the panel can't be reached.
Hand-uploaded mods on panel servers show their real name and version.
The What's new button in the update notice sits next to Update now.
fixed: Codex chat failed when the Codex app was set to a model the command line can't use, and couldn't use the app's tools.
The settings search bar covered dialogs opened from Server settings.

added: Reports which chunks are loaded and which are force-loaded, every 5 seconds.
Monolab first release.
